reviewer: Model author; separate release review remains required
method: Individually viewed all eight retained exterior photographs, two architect section drawings and actual official PDF pages 6–11 before geometry. Individually viewed all nine final actual renders and compared front, two different theater sides, rear/screens, whole plan/roof, roof slot, facade rhythm, Globe joins, supports and ramp centers.
findings: Whole connected cube and three distinct projecting theater masses retained; Grand is asymmetric and roof higher than lower rectangular Blue Box.
Globe intersects front cube and has two slanted supports, not isolated ball.
Rear contains two high open-top screen towers and stepped/recessed central service faces.
Main roof and Blue Box roof contain visible-family planted/paved layout with circles; central roof slot has actual depression and crossing braces.
Open ground perimeter and under-theater gaps remain; neutral base does not fill them.
Initial side platform rectangles filled portions of loop centers; removed after actual source-vs-top/rear render review. Both final ramp centers are open and descending decks have real geometry.
Source-grounded color families appear in actual geometry render with no textures, source pixels or baked lighting. Silver is not interpreted as gold despite warm lighting in some source photos.
known_approximations: Normalized proportions only; no verified dimensions or exact building scale.
Roof paths/circles, panel seams, corrugation counts, screen relief and stair mesh generalized.
Ramp paths/slopes approximate; source platform outline was simplified to the visible rear strip and loops, not a site/accessibility survey.
Roof-slot floor and solid exterior volumes are closure conventions; no hidden interior or service equipment claims.
Individual source capture dates unknown; 2022 refers to completion/design context, not exact photograph year.
